Things are getting super Muslim weird in NYC.
A couple of nights ago I was at a Michelin starred Spanish restaurant off Union Square with my 60-something year old friend, a sweet, soft-spoken, churchgoing lady who’d been my late mom’s home health aide for years.
We were speaking quietly, as we always do, and the restaurant is small and loud at dinner time.
I was looking at the menu for dessert wines & told my girlfriend, “I want a Spanish wine, not from an area that uses Moroccan labor”.
Within a minute the manager arrived with the check and said, “Leave right now!” 
Shocked, I asked, “Why?”.
No such thing had ever happened to me in my life.
He said, “You were speaking ill of Muslims!”
I said, “I was looking at the wine menu”.
“Leave right now!”, he yelled in front of the other customers, who stared in surprise themselves.
We were so shocked & ashamed to be getting kicked out of a restaurant, that I just clicked my usual 30% tip on the screen and we left.
They’d even charged us for desserts we never got before we were kicked out.
This at a Michelin starred restaurant in Manhattan, all because I quietly told my friend I wanted a Spanish wine not from an area where they use Moroccan labor.
It’s getting very weird and bad in Manhattan.

NIGERIANS, WE NEED YOUR HELP! 🇳🇬

INEC has restricted the amount of time each person can spend on its website, so we need as many people as possible to help with this exercise.

Here’s what we’re doing:

We’re counting the number of registered voters in each polling unit for 2027 and comparing it with the number of registered voters in that same polling unit in 2023.

INEC won’t show us the full register, so we have to do this ourselves, one polling unit at a time.

Here’s how you can help. It takes just 60 seconds!

STEP 1: Go to this link ⤵️

https://t.co/Yo17bPEiad

STEP 2: Copy the code generated where it says “Your Polling Unit”. It’s the code containing numbers and dashes.

STEP 3: Go to the INEC website and scroll down to “Find a Polling Unit”.

Paste the code you copied into the PU Code box and click “Find”.

STEP 4: The polling unit information will appear, including the number of registered voters.

Copy ONLY the number of registered voters (the whole number, without the dashes).

STEP 5: Return to the first website, paste the number into the space provided for registered voters and click Submit.

That’s all!

See the attached video for a visual guide.

60 seconds of your time can help us build a clearer picture of what’s happening with our voters’ register.

Please participate and share this with other Nigerians. The more people who help, the more polling units we can cover.
